item.title: Myanmar's civil war: the situation
item.description:
The Myanmar army has stepped up large-scale strikes, hitting a Naga insurgent camp and killing 36 fighters, and conducting airstrikes that wounded one person near a hospital in Myebon and killed seven civilians in Sin Ai Village, Pauktaw Township. The junta is enforcing strict conscription quotas, prompting youths to fear abduction for forced service, while militant groups have desecrated a Christian place of worship. The United States has opened direct talks with Myanmar’s generals and lifted sanctions on the daughter of a military-linked businessman, and Min Aung Hlaing met Malaysian officials. Health-care facilities continued to be attacked, as documented for 16‑30 September 2026. The conflict caused 2,332 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

Machine-written from the linked sources, checked for figures and names not in them.
